discrepancies.topic: autocomplete loop variable is never declared

a.value: autocomplete.html: 'for (word of WORDS) {' with no let/const

b.value: node 20: the loop works in non-strict code by creating an implicit global named word; the same loop under 'use strict' throws ReferenceError (box run 2026-10-29). MDN for...of shows 'for (const element of array)'

discrepancies.note: Code kept verbatim in w08-n15; an authored callout explains the implicit global and shows the declared form 'for (let word of WORDS)' as the habit to keep.

discrepancies.topic: 'the center attribute cascades'

a.value: 'Because everything inside body is a child of body, the center attribute cascades down to those children.'

b.value: Same section: 'CSS is filled with properties'; text-align: center is a CSS property set through the style attribute

discrepancies.note: Persian note says the text-align property (set in the style attribute) is inherited by the children.

discrepancies.topic: 'Semantic tags' bullet describes classes and the style element

a.value: 'It turns out that there are newer semantic tags included in HTML' followed by an explanation of the <style> element and class selectors

b.value: home4.html itself shows both: header, main and footer (semantic tags) and the classes centered, large, medium, small

discrepancies.note: w08-n11 treats the two ideas separately: semantic tags (header/main/footer) and class selectors in a <style> element.

discrepancies.topic: Who is to blame for a 500

a.value: '500 errors are usually your fault as the developer when they concern a product or application of your creation' (with a caveat about infrastructure and third parties)

b.value: '500 Internal Server Error ... it's not actually you making a mistake in your request. It's actually the server failing'

discrepancies.note: Different points of view: the short speaks to the visitor making the request, the notes to the developer of the server. The Persian note states both.

discrepancies.topic: Homepage starter head adds jQuery; the lecture's Bootstrap head does not

a.value: starter index.html head links bootstrap@5.3.8 CSS and JS and also https://code.jquery.com/jquery-4.0.0.js

b.value: Bootstrap head in the notes has only the two bootstrap@5.3.8 tags; Bootstrap 5 does not need jQuery

discrepancies.note: Guide says jQuery is included by the starter and is optional; nothing in Week 8 requires it. The DOM short (2017) presents jQuery as the most popular library of its time.

discrepancies.topic: Radio Shack Redo links Bootstrap 5.2 docs

a.value: navbar, columns, images and carousel links go to getbootstrap.com/docs/5.2/

b.value: notes and Homepage use bootstrap@5.3.8 and docs/5.3

discrepancies.note: Redo is the 2022 lab; the guide links the 5.3 pages next to the official 5.2 links and says the class names used there are the same in 5.3 (inference, labelled).

discrepancies.topic: Typos in Radio Shack Redo

a.value: 'aquainted', 'controling', 'Scoll', 'appropriage'

b.value: intended: acquainted, controlling, Scroll, appropriate

discrepancies.note: Typos only; any quoted requirement text keeps the original spelling.

discrepancies.topic: Official Trivia page shows full staff solutions

a.value: The How to Submit section includes two complete staff solutions (the multiple-choice and free-response handlers with the correct answers)

b.value: Package rule FR-13 / D64: no solution content; the CS50 honesty policy forbids copying solutions

discrepancies.note: The staff solutions are link-only in the Persian Trivia guide; validate.py forbids the solution's distinctive strings anywhere in week-08 (D64).

discrepancies.topic: Internet Primer: IPv6 'eight clusters of 16 bytes'

a.value: 'we now have eight clusters of 16 bytes. And 8 times 16 is 128.'

b.value: IPv6 addresses are 128 bits; eight groups of 16 bits (the short's own arithmetic, 8 x 16 = 128, only works for bits)

discrepancies.note: Slip of the tongue; the Persian short page says 16 bits per group.

discrepancies.topic: Shorts are 2017 recordings for an older CS50 (PHP, var, jQuery, getElementById)

a.value: 'websites ... written in ... PHP'; JavaScript short uses var for local variables; DOM short uses getElementById and jQuery ('probably the most popular JavaScript library currently in use')

b.value: CS50x 2026 uses Python/Flask on the server (Week 9), let in JavaScript, document.querySelector, and no jQuery

discrepancies.note: Each Persian short page has a note mapping the 2017 forms to the 2026 ones (let instead of var, querySelector instead of getElementById).

discrepancies.topic: JavaScript short: array 'size method', srcElement, 'everything is an object'

a.value: 'we can call the size method, or pop, or push, or shift'; the event example reads the event's source element; 'in JavaScript, everything is a special case of an object. ... var x equals 44 - that's an object'

b.value: Arrays have a length property, not a size method; the standard property is event.target (srcElement is a legacy alias); numbers and strings are primitive values, not objects

discrepancies.note: Persian short page uses length and event.target and calls 44 a primitive value (authored correction, labelled).

discrepancies.topic: HTML short: DOCTYPE and 'self-closing' tags

a.value: '[the doctype] can be omitted but ... you can't use any of the tags that are HTML5 tags'; input and img described as self-closing with a slash before >

b.value: Without <!DOCTYPE html> browsers render in quirks mode, but new elements still parse; img and input are void elements and the trailing slash is optional in HTML

discrepancies.note: Persian short page: always write <!DOCTYPE html> (as the lecture does) because it selects standards mode; void elements need no end tag and no slash. Lecture examples use no slash.

discrepancies.topic: TCP short transcript: 'connection with protocol'

a.value: 'which can happen because IP is a connection with protocol and so different packets can take different paths'

b.value: IP moves each packet independently; the intended word is 'connectionless'

discrepancies.note: Transcription slip in the official .txt; Persian page says IP is connectionless (inference from context, labelled).

discrepancies.topic: 'Every computer has a unique address in the world'

a.value: 'Every computer has a unique address in the world.'

b.value: 'something called a private IP address ... funneling them through one single address, which is shared by many different computers'

discrepancies.note: Persian note keeps the official idea and adds, from the short, that home devices usually share one public address through a router.

discrepancies.topic: pattern=".+@.+\.edu" 'must include an @ symbol and a .edu'

a.value: 'the email address must include an @ symbol and a .edu'

b.value: The pattern attribute must match the whole value: in jsdom malan@harvard.edu passes, malan@harvard.edu.com and a@b.edux fail (box run 2026-10-29)

discrepancies.note: Persian note: the value must END with .edu, because pattern is matched against the entire value.

b.value: homepage.zip from cdn.cs50.net/2026/x/psets/8/; redo.zip from cdn.cs50.net/2022/fall/labs/8/

a.value: download links cover hello0, paragraphs, headings, lists0, lists1, table, image, video, link0, search0-1, register0-1, home0, home3, home4, home7, phonebook0-1, hello1, hello3, hello5, background, blink, autocomplete

discrepancies.topic: HTML short: h1-h6 'progressively larger'

a.value: 'six different levels of headers ... which are progressively larger and larger headers. And they get smaller and smaller'

b.value: h1 is the top-level (largest) heading; h6 the smallest

discrepancies.note: Speaker corrects himself in the next sentence; the Persian page states h1 largest to h6 smallest.

discrepancies.topic: Section 8: '=== for strict equality' but scoreboard.html uses ==

a.value: Kelly: equality 'will be checked using 3 equal signs for strict equality', then shows that == behaves the same here and = alerts immediately

b.value: scoreboard.html (src8.zip): if (team1 == 10) and if (team2 == 10)

discrepancies.note: Both work for numbers; the Persian section page quotes the file as published and recommends === (as in the lecture and notes).

discrepancies.topic: Section 8: 'em ... calculates based on the size of your screen'

a.value: 'this EM ... is this sort of relative measurement which calculates based on the size of your screen'

b.value: em is relative to the element's font size (screen-relative units are vw/vh)

discrepancies.note: Persian page: em is relative to the font size (inference from the CSS reference; not run on the box).

discrepancies.topic: Section 8: 'light blue does not exist'

a.value: 'light blue does not exist' (typed with a space), then a student notes 'lightblue without a space exists'

b.value: scoreboard.html: background-color: lightblue;

discrepancies.note: Persian page: CSS colour names are single words without spaces (lightblue).

discrepancies.topic: HTTP short: version is 'probably always going to be HTTP/1.1'

a.value: 'HTTP version is probably always going to be HTTP/1.1. 1.0 also exists but isn't really used anymore.'

b.value: the lecture's request/response examples use HTTP/2

discrepancies.note: 2017 recording; the Persian short page notes that the 2025 lecture shows HTTP/2.

discrepancies.topic: CSS short: border style 'ridge ... would be wavy line'; opacity called a tag

a.value: 'a ridge line, which would be wavy line'; 'opacity, which is a tag we didn't talk about'

b.value: ridge draws a 3D ridged border; opacity is a CSS property

discrepancies.note: Persian page corrects both (inference from the CSS reference; not rendered on the box).
